clue.text: Anxious, perhaps even worried about one

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the single letter
something worried is shaken about, so the letters of perhaps and even are jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone nervous, maybe even fretting over one particular thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges PERHAPSEVEN; 'about' wraps that around I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person filled with dread or unease about the future is anxious.

clue.text: Zeppelin tune's welcome on piano

parts.note: a tune is an air; the possessive gives airs, read as 'air is' contracted
hi is a word of welcome, a greeting
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A Led Zeppelin song gets a warm reception when played on the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeppelin looks like the rock band; here it is the German dirigible.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zeppelin is a rigid dirigible balloon, the classic example of a lighter-than-air craft.

clue.text: One prints articles perhaps enraging readers initially

definitions.text: One prints articles perhaps enraging readers initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A publication runs stories that may anger the people who read them.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'prints articles perhaps enraging readers' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is something that prints articles which may well enrage its readership.

clue.text: Take out bird in exclusive surroundings

indicators.note: in places the bird within the other word
surroundings says the exclusive word forms the setting round the bird

parts.note: elite means exclusive, select
mina is a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Shooting a bird in a posh, private setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'surroundings' both signal containment; the bird is a variant spelling of myna, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to take out a rival or target is to remove or kill it entirely.

clue.text: English cow perhaps produces cheese

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, a cow being one example

explanation.surface: An English cow makes cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the cow as just one example of a dam, a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese sold in red-waxed rounds, an example of the category.

clue.text: Furtive and bashful, embracing bird on time

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the bashful word wraps the bird and time

parts.note: bashful means shy
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A timid, secretive person cuddling a bird, and punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps the bashful word around the duck and time together; 'on' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: furtive behaviour is sly, sneaky and done to avoid being noticed.

clue.text: Harm one violently bottling up poison

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the concealed letters are read from bottom to top
bottling means holding inside, so the letters are concealed within these words

explanation.surface: Hurting someone brutally while keeping an angry spite pent up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottling' takes MONEV from 'harM ONE Violently'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the toxin a snake or spider injects is poison, the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Reputation still rising

definitions.meaning: one's status or esteem among others
not moving, as of stagnant water

explanation.surface: A good name that keeps on climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate definitions of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Status, motionless water, and getting up off a seat are all senses of the one word.

clue.text: In lay-by, go near to get past

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Pull into a lay-by and creep near to overtake.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside parking bay; 'past' seems the overtaking but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something bygone belongs to a former time, over and done with.

clue.text: Clone particle spinning around electron briefly

indicators.note: around says the jumble goes round the next piece
spinning sets the letters of particle whirling into a new order

parts.note: E is the shortened form, the symbol, for an electron

explanation.surface: A physicist copies a particle whose spin circles an electron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' rearranges PARTICLE; 'around' puts that round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone something is to make an exact copy of it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Sharp old negative contains edges of tint

indicators.note: contains means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: nay is an archaic word for no

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of the word tint

explanation.surface: An old photographic negative with a crisp, tinted border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old negative' sounds photographic but is NAY, archaic no.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp in the sense of smartly dressed; a dapper, trim appearance.

clue.text: Solitary island faces empty inlet

parts.note: Herm is one of the Channel Islands

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of the word, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lonely island looks out over a dry creek.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is a small Channel Island; 'Solitary' is a noun here, a recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary, as a noun, is a recluse who lives alone, away from society.

clue.text: Dance with passion joining new company

parts.note: a flame is a burning passion

explanation.surface: A troupe newly joined performs a dance full of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fiery Spanish style of Andalusian dancing with stamping and guitar.

clue.text: Aspen is common without upper-class

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: popular means common, of the people
U is the classic label for upper-class

explanation.surface: The aspen is a common tree, not the posh sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Aspen looks like the Colorado resort; it is a tree of the same genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen belongs to the genus Populus, so it is a kind of this tree.

clue.text: Realist oddly supports Left in painting

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it follows

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A realist painter backs the political left in their art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes RAIT from Realist; 'supports' puts it under PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a painting of a person, typically showing the face, is a likeness of this kind.

clue.text: One's in rush after Conservative whip, say

indicators.note: after puts the Conservative letter first, followed by the rest
in places the next letters inside the rush word

parts.note: haste means rush, hurry
one is I, and 's is is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A Tory party whip hurrying after a member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is I'S; 'say' marks whipping as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: whipping is one way to punish severely, the classic form of physical rebuke.

clue.text: Bit unwell encased by cast in suffering

indicators.note: encased by means held inside the jumbled letters
suffering signals the letters of cast in are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Feeling a little sick while stuck in a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges the six letters of 'cast in' to SCINTA; 'encased by' puts the unwell word inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tiny trace or iota, the smallest bit of something.

clue.text: Weapons companies checking each rifle's tip

indicators.note: checking means holding back, restraining, so the firms word holds the others inside

parts.note: firms are companies

indicators.note: tip picks the leading letter of the word rifle

explanation.surface: Arms makers inspect every rifle's tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checking' looks like inspection but means restraining, so containing; 'tip' takes the rifle's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: guns, pistols and rifles are weapons carried by hand.

clue.text: Alternative drainage needed for plant

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters of drainage is wanted

explanation.surface: A different drainage system is required for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a works needing drainage; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fragrant white-flowered evergreen shrub of the coffee family.

clue.text: Cinders follows Charming's rear and splits

indicators.note: follows puts the Cinders piece after the other
rear picks the final letter of the word Charming

parts.note: cinders are ashes

explanation.surface: Cinderella tags behind Prince Charming, then they break up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders and Charming are from the pantomime Cinderella, but here cinders are ASHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: gashes are long deep cuts, splits or slashes in a surface.

clue.text: Chaste but gettin' close, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the spoken form matters

parts.note: verging, with the dropped g, means getting close

explanation.surface: Someone pure, yet edging nearer, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: VERGIN' (verging, close to) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone chaste has never had sex, the adjective sense.

clue.text: No bother about figure

parts.note: taken as written
nag means bother, pester
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: It's no trouble to deal with a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a geometric figure with nine sides and nine angles.

clue.text: One runs small computer peripheral

parts.note: a printer is a device attached to a computer

explanation.surface: A little printer is set running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One runs' looks like machinery working; it is an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is an athlete who races short distances, someone who runs.

clue.text: Country's queen mostly coming from the south

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue coming from the south means read upwards
mostly removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A nation's queen mostly arrives from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts REGINA to REGIN; 'coming from the south' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a landlocked West African nation named after its great river.

clue.text: Pull head of radish stuck in soil

indicators.note: stuck in places the letter inside the soil word

parts.note: to soil is to stain or dirty

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of radish

explanation.surface: Pulling up a radish buried in the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soil' looks like earth; it is the verb, STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to pull a muscle is to strain it, the injury sense.

clue.text: Excuse of a party, formerly independent

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal Party, merged into the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A politician's excuse: they were once with a party, now independent.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere when a crime was committed, so an excuse.

clue.text: Part of stove, naturally

indicators.note: part of says a stretch of letters sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Of course an oven is part of a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'stOVE Naturally', and the clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking range or stove usually includes an enclosed compartment for baking and roasting.

clue.text: Looking at some money in gamble

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eyeing a portion of the cash staked on a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: watching closely, looking at something with interest.

clue.text: Flipping partner can start to get repulsive

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the partner word is read backwards

parts.note: a lover is a partner
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of get

explanation.surface: An angry partner can start getting nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse but reverses LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something revolting is disgusting, so repulsive.

clue.text: Show possibly entertains with endless pop

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters could be arranged another way
endless drops the final letter of pop

explanation.surface: A show may well entertain, with non-stop pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts pop to PO; 'possibly' rearranges ENTERTAINS plus PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a show or display put on for an audience, a formal demonstration.
